sections.text: ## Vladimir Ilyich Lenin (1870–1924)

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: ### The Theory: Vanguard Party

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: Marxism predicted that the working class (*proletariat*) would develop "class consciousness" — understand their exploitation and organize politically. In practice, Russian workers were developing trade union consciousness (better wages and conditions) rather than revolutionary consciousness (overthrow of capitalism). Lenin's *What Is to Be Done?* (1902) argued that left to themselves, workers would only achieve "trade union consciousness." The revolution required a *vanguard party* of professional revolutionaries — intellectuals who understood Marxist theory and could lead the workers.

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara
Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
Orthodox Marxism:
  Proletariat → develops class consciousness → organizes →
  revolution (inevitable through economic forces)

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
Leninism:
  Vanguard Party → educates and leads proletariat →
  organizes workers + peasants → seizes power →
  "dictatorship of the proletariat" (transitional state)
  → eventually withers away (never happened)

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
Key features:
  - Democratic centralism: debate within party; unity in action
  - Professional full-time revolutionaries
  - Underground organization (necessary under Tsarist repression)
  - Party disciplines individual members

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
Consequence: the party IS the revolution; the party cannot
  be questioned; the party's survival = the revolution's survival
  This logic led directly to the Cheka (secret police),
  Red Terror, and eventually Stalin's apparatus.
```

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: ### The October Revolution (November 7, 1917 — Old Style Calendar: October 25)

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: WWI had destroyed the Romanov regime. The February Revolution (March 1917 in modern calendar) produced a Provisional Government (constitutional liberals + socialists) but it continued the war. The Soviets (workers' councils) held independent power. Lenin arrived from Swiss exile in April 1917 (Germany facilitated his travel — they wanted Russia out of the war).

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: Lenin's *April Theses*: Bolsheviks should not support the Provisional Government; they should call for immediate peace, land redistribution, and transfer of power to soviets. The slogan: "Peace, Land, Bread."

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: **The seizure of power** was a coup, not a mass revolution. The Military Revolutionary Committee of the Petrograd Soviet, controlled by Trotsky, seized key communications and infrastructure. The Provisional Government dissolved without significant resistance. It was over in hours.

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: **Lenin's Responsibility**: Lenin built the one-party state, the Cheka, the Red Terror, and the logic that the party's survival justified any violence. Stalin used that apparatus at a scale Lenin had not. Whether Stalin was Lenin's "logical conclusion" or a divergence from Lenin's vision is contested. Lenin did try to warn against Stalin personally. He had already built the structure Stalin would operate.

sections.text: ## Mao Zedong (1893–1976)

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: ### The Strategic Innovations

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: Mao's theoretical contribution to revolutionary politics: adapting Leninism to a peasant society. Russia had an industrial proletariat; China in 1921 did not. Mao argued that the peasantry could be the revolutionary class if properly organized.

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
```
  MAO'S PEASANT WAR THEORY
  =========================

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
Lenin: urban workers + revolutionary party
  Mao:   rural peasants + party + people's army
         "Political power grows out of the barrel of a gun"

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
Three phases of People's War:
  1. Strategic defense: guerrillas in base areas; avoid decisive battles
  2. Strategic stalemate: build strength; expand liberated zones
  3. Strategic offensive: conventional forces attack and win

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
The Long March (1934-35):
  KMT encirclement → CCP abandons Jiangxi Soviet
  6,000 miles on foot; 100,000 started, 8,000-10,000 finished
  Mao consolidates leadership during the march
  → Yan'an base area; develops theory; consolidates party control

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
Anti-Japanese War (1937-45):
  CCP and KMT both fight Japan
  CCP uses war to expand base areas from SE China to N. China
  KMT bleeds fighting Japan; CCP expands
  → Civil War resumes 1946; CCP wins 1949
```

sections.text: **The People's Republic (1949–1976)**:

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
| Period | Policy | Deaths | Economic effect |
|--------|--------|--------|-----------------|
| 1950–52 | Land Reform | 1–2M landlords killed | Land redistributed |
| 1950–53 | Korean War | 180,000 Chinese KIA | International isolation |
| 1956–57 | Hundred Flowers Campaign | — | Intellectuals lured into criticizing party |
| 1957–58 | Anti-Rightist Campaign | 300,000 labeled "rightists" | Intellectuals purged |
| 1958–62 | Great Leap Forward | 30–45M dead (famine) | Industrial + agricultural collapse |
| 1966–76 | Cultural Revolution | 0.5–2M killed; millions persecuted | Cultural destruction; economic disruption |
| 1976 | Mao dies | — | Deng Xiaoping opens reforms |

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: **The Great Leap Forward** is the deadliest policy failure in human history in terms of direct death toll. Mao mandated steel production through backyard furnaces (which produced useless pig iron), requiring peasants to abandon harvests. Grain production collapsed. Local officials falsified production figures upward because reporting failure meant punishment. Famine resulted. Mao knew by 1959; continued the policy for two more years.

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: ### Mao's Lasting Influence

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
The legacy outside China is as a theory and symbol more than as a model:
- Maoist movements: Peru (Sendero Luminoso), Nepal (Maoist insurgency that transformed into coalition government), India (Naxalites)
- "Maoism" in 1960s–70s Western student movements: revolutionary romanticism; Cultural Revolution as anti-establishment
- China since 1978: economic reforms under Deng explicitly rejected Maoist economics; the CCP maintains political continuity with Mao while rejecting most of his economic program

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: Xi Jinping has rehabilitated Mao's image for domestic legitimacy purposes while maintaining Deng's economic model — an unstable combination.

sections.text: ## Ernesto "Che" Guevara (1928–1967)

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: ### What He Did

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: Guevara was an Argentine physician who became a Marxist revolutionary through his *Motorcycle Diaries* tour of Latin America (1952), witnessing poverty and a CIA-backed coup (Guatemala, 1954). He joined Castro's Cuban revolutionary movement in Mexico in 1955.

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: **Cuba (1956–59)**: Guevara led the guerrilla column that was decisive in the battle for Santa Clara (December 28, 1958). Castro entered Havana on January 8, 1959. Batista had fled New Year's Eve.

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: **Post-revolution role**: As head of the National Bank of Cuba and Minister of Industry, Guevara attempted to industrialize Cuba on a Soviet model. The results were poor (sugar production collapsed; industrialization failed; Cuba became dependent on Soviet subsidies).

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: **Foco theory**:

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara
Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
Orthodox Leninism: vanguard party first → build mass support →
                     revolutionary situation → insurrection

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
Foco theory:       small guerrilla group ("foco") establishes
                     itself in favorable terrain → actions create
                     revolutionary situation → masses follow

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
Key claims:
  1. You don't need to wait for "objective conditions"
  2. The guerrilla band itself creates the conditions
  3. Rural base + mountain terrain + moral example
  4. "The duty of every revolutionary is to make the revolution"

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
PRACTICAL RECORD:
  Cuba (1956-59): worked (special conditions — Batista's
    weak regime; US pressure; Havana organized support)
  Bolivia (1966-67): failed completely
    - Peasants didn't support the foreign guerrillas
    - Party discipline broke down
    - CIA + Bolivian Army located and killed the group
    October 9, 1967: Guevara captured and executed

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
The Cuban success was not a generalizable model.
  The conditions that made Cuba work didn't apply elsewhere.
```

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: ### Guevara as Symbol

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
Guevara the symbol (Alberto Korda's 1960 photograph; the t-shirt) diverged completely from Guevara the actual political theorist. The symbol represents romantic revolutionary spirit, anti-imperialism, anti-corporate sentiment. The actual person:
- Supervised execution of hundreds in Cuba after the revolution
- Argued for nuclear confrontation with the US (during the Cuban Missile Crisis he wanted the missiles used)
- Applied command economy theory with poor results
- Died in a military failure in Bolivia

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: The gap between the romantic image and the historical figure is one of the largest in modern political iconography.

sections.text: ## Fidel Castro (1926–2016)

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: ### The Revolution

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: Castro organized the attack on the Moncada Barracks (July 26, 1953) — the birth of the 26th of July Movement. The attack failed; Castro was imprisoned, then amnestied, then exiled to Mexico. There he met Guevara. He landed in Cuba with 82 men on the *Granma* in December 1956; most were killed immediately; 12–20 survivors including Castro and Guevara fled to the Sierra Maestra mountains.

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: The two-year guerrilla campaign was effective less because of military victories and more because the Batista regime was losing support across Cuban society — urban underground, labor, middle class, even military elements. Batista fled December 31, 1958.

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
```
  CUBAN REVOLUTION: KEY FACTS VS. POPULAR MISCONCEPTION
  =======================================================

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
MISCONCEPTION: Guerrilla war in the mountains won
  REALITY: Urban underground (llano) and middle-class
           opposition (students, urban workers, professional
           class) was as important as the Sierra Maestra
           campaign. Castro coordinated both.

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
MISCONCEPTION: Castro always planned a communist state
  REALITY: He explicitly denied Communist alignment until
           after the Bay of Pigs (1961). The turn to
           Soviet alignment was partly driven by US hostility
           (Bay of Pigs, assassination attempts, embargo).

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
MISCONCEPTION: Cuba's healthcare and literacy gains
                 justify the political system
  REALITY: Cuba did achieve near-universal literacy (1961
           campaign) and functional healthcare. The economy
           stagnated; political repression was real
           (UMAP labor camps for gays, dissidents, etc.);
           200,000+ political prisoners over the decades.
           Outcomes on some social metrics ≠ justification
           for the political system.
```

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
**Castro's Institutional Achievement**: Castro built a stable one-party state that survived:
- Bay of Pigs invasion (1961)
- CIA assassination attempts (600+, reportedly)
- US trade embargo (1962–present)
- Soviet collapse (1991) — the "Special Period" of severe deprivation
- Transition to Raúl Castro (2008) and Miguel Díaz-Canel (2018) — maintained system continuity beyond the founder

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text: This institutional durability is unusual for a Latin American revolution. Most didn't survive their founders.

sections.text: ## Comparison Table

metadata.title: Revolutionary Leaders: Lenin, Mao, Castro, Guevara

sections.text:
| Figure | Method | State Built | Death Toll (Policy) | Durability |
|--------|--------|-------------|---------------------|------------|
| Lenin | Urban coup; party vanguard | Soviet one-party state | Red Terror: 50,000-200,000; civil war famine: 5M | State lasted 74 years (to 1991) |
| Mao | Peasant war; united front | Chinese one-party state | Land reform + Great Leap: 30-50M; Cultural Revolution: 1-2M | CCP still in power |
| Castro | Guerrilla + urban underground | Cuban one-party state | Post-revolution executions; political repression | State continues under successors |
| Guevara | Foco theory; direct action | N/A (died 1967) | — | Largely a symbol; foco theory refuted |
